implementation: Todo 1 - Fixed corpus manifest and explicit bootstrap/verification contract

dependencyBlocked.make_e2e_live: No Makefile target 'e2e-live' exists in this repository. Task notes: 'only if the target exists from another lane, otherwise record as dependency-blocked.'

malformed_input.result: Both return exit code 2 (missing flag) or 1 (MISSING_ROOT)

stale_state.result: DRIFT_DETECTED with exit code 1, exit code 0 after re-bootstrap

classes: no runtime files tracked — runner.mjs, manifest.json, corpus/ are tracked by git
dirty_worktree.result: Verified committed manifest and corpus are tracked; temp root dirs are ephemeral

classes: verify returns exit code 0 only after hash match
manifest entry SHA-256 verified in test
misleading_success_output.result: exit code 0 requires all SHA-256 matches; any mismatch yields exit code 1

missing_manifest.reason: Not applicable — manifest is part of the fixture repo files, not created by bootstrap. verify-corpus throws MANIFEST_MISSING if manifest.json is absent from the fixture root (scripts/live-e2e/). Bootstrap fails with MANIFEST_MISSING before writing anything.

empty_corpus.reason: Not applicable — corpus has exactly one entry and manifest is versioned. Empty corpus would mean empty entries array, which would pass verify (no files to check), but bootstrap would create no files. Not an adversarial class for a fixed fixture.

concurrent_bootstrap.reason: Out of scope for Todo 1. Bootstrap is idempotent; concurrent calls to mkdirSync + copyFileSync on the same root are safe at the OS level.

permission_denied.reason: Not tested; would require altering filesystem permissions. Verification would fail with EACCES on readFileSync, which surfaces as a raw error.

postWriteReview.singleResponsibility: scripts/live-e2e/ owns one thing: fixed live-e2e fixture corpus manifest + bootstrap/verify tooling. runner.mjs is the entrypoint, manifest.json is the data contract, corpus/ is the fixture files.
postWriteReview.boundaryPurity: Root path from CLI is a string — it's resolved and validated at the boundary (existsSync). The manifest is parsed from JSON into a typed object. All external input (CLI args, file reads) is validated at the boundary.
postWriteReview.variantDiscrimination: No discriminated union switches. The CLI command is switched via a simple string match with an explicit default case — appropriate here since it's not a tagged type from a data model.
postWriteReview.defensiveLayer: None. The runner trusts readFileSync/copyFileSync with proper error propagation. No unnecessary null checks.
postWriteReview.helpersForOneOff: None. copyManifestFile is used twice (manifest + entries) — shared helper is appropriate.
postWriteReview.tests: 7 tests cover manifest structural validity, SHA-256 integrity, bootstrap idempotence, verify pass/fail, missing root, and drift detection.
postWriteReview.redundantVerification: None. Bootstrap writes files; verify-corpus reads them. No post-action re-query.
postWriteReview.negativeNaming: None. All names are positive (verifyCorpus, bootstrap, loadManifest).
postWriteReview.loggingConventions: Runner uses console.log/console.error with structured prefix tags (BOOTSTRAP_OK, VERIFY_OK, VERIFY_FAIL). Follows project existing pattern of prefix-based output.
